findings.description: values.sort() uses default lexicographic ordering and mutates the caller's array in place, producing wrong medians and side effects.
findings.scenario: median([10, 9, 2]) sorts as [10, 2, 9] and returns 2 instead of 9; caller's array is also reordered.

findings.description: average divides by values.length with no empty check, returning NaN for empty arrays, which the comment says is legitimate.
var i is shared across the timeout callbacks; by the time they fire i === jobs.length, so run receives undefined for every job.
findings.fix: Use `for (let i = 0; ...)` or capture jobs[i] in a const per iteration.

findings.description: median of an empty array returns NaN ((undefined + undefined)/2).
percentile on empty input returns undefined (index -1), and the index method is nearest-rank-ish without validation of p.
findings.scenario: percentile([], 50) returns undefined; p<0 gives idx negative -> undefined.
findings.fix: Guard empty input and clamp idx with Math.max(0, ...).
